findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the Maven cache persistence mechanism: specify whether it is a named Docker volume or a host bind-mount, explain how it survives `docker compose down -v` in CI (e.g. use `--volumes` omission or a `actions/cache` step for `~/.m2`), and add the chosen mechanism to scope and the relevant AC.

findings.finding: The plan requires a persistent Maven cache volume to avoid re-downloading ~900 artifacts, but the CI teardown is explicitly modelled on the langfuse-trace job's `docker compose ... down -v`. The `-v` flag removes named Docker volumes, which would destroy a named Maven cache volume on every teardown — making the cache useless across CI runs. A bind-mount of `~/.m2` is not destroyed by `down -v` but GitHub Actions runners do not persist `~/.m2` between jobs without an explicit `actions/cache` step, which is absent from the plan's scope. The plan never specifies whether the Maven cache is a named volume, a bind mount, or a cached host path, nor how it survives across separate CI job invocations.
findings.location: Approach section — 'The fixture SHOULD mount a persistent Maven cache (~/.m2) as a volume'; Scope — 'a NEW, SEPARATE job, modelled on the langfuse-trace job ... docker compose ... down -v under if: always()'
scenarios: CI job runs, Maven cache accumulates in a named volume, teardown runs `down -v`, volume is deleted; next CI run re-downloads all 900+ artifacts — persistent cache provides zero benefit across runs.

Maven cache is implemented as a bind mount of `~/.m2`; `down -v` doesn't destroy it, but the GHA runner's `~/.m2` is empty at job start without an `actions/cache` step — same result: every run re-downloads.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) omit `-v` from the teardown step to preserve the named Maven cache volume between CI runs on the same runner (and note this in the README as a maintenance consideration), or (b) add an `actions/cache` step in the new workflow job that caches `~/.m2` keyed on the Jira version, and use a host bind-mount (`- ~/.m2:/root/.m2`) instead of a named volume so the GHA cache populates it. Document the chosen approach in scope and add an AC that the Maven cache survives teardown for the purpose of the next run.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the Maven cache volume type (named Docker volume vs. host bind-mount), state the retirement trigger (e.g. a `jira-dc-clean` Makefile target or a periodic CI prune step), and add a note in the compose file or README documenting whether `down -v` removes it — resolving the ambiguity that makes caching and cleanup mutually exclusive under the current spec.

findings.finding: The Maven cache volume's lifecycle is underspecified in a way that creates both a state-accumulation problem and a concurrency-safety gap. The plan says to 'mount a persistent Maven cache (~/.m2) as a volume' but does not resolve whether this is a named Docker volume or a host bind-mount. If a named Docker volume: `down -v` (specified in the CI teardown step) destroys it on every run, defeating its purpose of avoiding re-downloads across runs. If a host bind-mount (`~/.m2`): (a) `down -v` does NOT remove it, so it accumulates ~900 artifacts per run indefinitely with no retirement path; (b) it is shared state with any other Maven-using process on the host; and (c) two concurrent `workflow_dispatch` triggers could cause Maven resolver conflicts on the same cache directory. Neither option has a stated ownership model, retirement trigger, or concurrency guard.
findings.location: Scope section, bullet 2: 'mounts a persistent Maven cache volume'; Approach section: 'The fixture SHOULD mount a persistent Maven cache (~/.m2) as a volume, or every fresh container re-downloads ~900 artifacts.'
scenarios: CI runner (ubuntu-latest): named Docker volume is wiped by `down -v` on teardown, so the next run re-downloads all 900 artifacts — the performance benefit the plan promises never materialises.

macOS developer workstation: host-mount of ~/.m2 accumulates Jira 8.17.1 Maven artifacts indefinitely; a developer running the harness monthly for a year retains hundreds of MBs of stale artifacts with no guidance on when or how to prune them.

Concurrent workflow_dispatch runs on a self-hosted runner or a runner pool sharing a workspace: two Maven processes writing to the same local repository simultaneously can corrupt artifact metadata, causing subsequent builds to fail with checksum errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a named Docker volume (e.g. `jira-maven-cache`) and explicitly do NOT pass `-v` to `down` in the CI teardown step (use `docker compose down` without `-v`), so the cache persists across runs. Add a separate `jira-dc-clean` Makefile target that runs `docker compose down -v` for when a full reset is needed. Document in the README that `jira-dc-clean` is the retirement path and that the volume is intentionally preserved by normal teardown.

findings.finding: The `make jira-dc-up` Makefile target and the `~/.m2` volume mount path in the compose file silently assume POSIX shell and Unix filesystem conventions, making the local-run path non-functional on a Windows developer workstation — a supported platform in rebar's matrix.

findings.location: Approach section ('Stated limitation, deliberately accepted') and Testing section ('happy path: ... raw REST v2'); code: acli_graph.py:227/328/422, acli_rest.py:183
scenarios: J6/J7 drives rebar's DC transport (AcliClient) against the 8.17.1 harness: get_parent_map, get_comment_map, get_issuelinks_map all call POST /rest/api/3/search/jql, which 8.17.1 does not expose — these calls will fail (likely 404) on the DC instance, meaning the harness cannot validate the adapter's bulk enrichment paths at all.
validate_assignee / resolve_reporter call GET /rest/api/3/user/search expecting accountId in response — DC 8.x returns name/key, not accountId, so identity resolution will misparse results.
